To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the velocity waveform in a slightly curved vessel can be described by a cosine function, that the cosine theta model is a good alternative for the Womersley approach to estimate blood volume flow, and that the velocity waveform measured at the position of maximum velocity rather than the centerline velocity waveform should be used to estimate the blood volume flow.
(i) the Womersley model is more accurate than the Poiseuille model, (ii) the cosine theta model is more accurate for slightly curved arteries than the Womersley and Poiseuille models.

(1) curvature of the vessel wall has a small effect on the estimation of the BVF, (2) using the velocity profile at the position where maximum velocity is observed instead of centerline velocity improves estimation accuracy, (3) the cosine theta model improves the accuracy of the BVF estimation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for non-invasive estimation of BVF from a single velocity waveform.
the development of a new method for the estimation of BVF in slightly curved arteries.
the assessment of blood volume flow (BVF) in slightly curved arteries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Womersley model is the most accurate model for the assessment of blood volume flow from velocity waveforms in curved arteries.
the Womersley and Poiseuille methods should be avoided and the CTM is the most accurate method if velocity profiles are available.
the CTM is the preferred choice for estimating BVF in slightly curved arteries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CTM is the most suitable for estimating BVF in slightly curved vessels, as long as velocity profiles are available.
we have shown that the influence of the curvature on the blood volume flow is significant, and that the cosine theta model is a better estimator than the Womersley and Poiseuille approach.
the cosine theta model is the preferred method to estimate BVF in slightly curved arteries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the influence of the curvature should be taken into account in BVF estimation methods.
the velocity waveform should be used to estimate BVF, rather than the centerline velocity.
the CTM is a promising approach for the non-invasive assessment of BVF, especially in slightly curved vessels, such as the brachial and carotid artery.
